passages.text: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD: “Listen to the words of this covenant and tell them to the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD gave Jeremiah a message.
The LORD said, “Listen to the words of this covenant.
Tell these words to the men of Judah.
Tell these words to the people who live in Jerusalem.”
passages.original: הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃ שִׁמְע֕וּ אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֖י הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את וְדִבַּרְתָּם֙ אֶל־ אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה וְעַל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: You must tell them that this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant, which I commanded your forefathers when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace, saying, ‘Obey Me, and do everything I command you, and you will be My people, and I will be your God.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD told Jeremiah to speak to the people.
The LORD said, “Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant.”
The LORD gave this covenant to the ancestors of Israel.
The LORD brought the ancestors out of the land of Egypt.
Egypt was a place of suffering, like an iron furnace.
The LORD commanded the ancestors, “Obey My voice.”
The LORD said, “Do everything I command you.”
The LORD said, “If you obey Me, you will be My people.”
The LORD said, “I will be your God.”
passages.original: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אָר֣וּר הָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁמַ֔ע אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֖י הַבְּרִ֥ית הַזֹּֽאת׃ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּ֣יתִי אֶת־ אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֡ם בְּי֣וֹם הוֹצִיאִֽי־ אוֹתָ֣ם מֵאֶֽרֶץ־ מִצְרַיִם֩ מִכּ֨וּר הַבַּרְזֶ֜ל לֵאמֹ֗ר שִׁמְע֤וּ בְקוֹלִי֙ וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם אוֹתָ֔ם כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ אֲצַוֶּ֖ה אֶתְכֶ֑ם וִהְיִ֤יתֶם לִי֙ לְעָ֔ם וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: This was in order to establish the oath I swore to your forefathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is to this day.” “Amen, LORD,” I answered.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD made a promise to the ancestors of the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
The LORD swore an oath to their forefathers.
The LORD promised to give them a land.
This land flows with milk and honey.
The LORD kept this promise until this day.
Jeremiah answered the LORD.
Jeremiah said, “Amen, LORD.”
passages.original: לְמַעַן֩ הָקִ֨ים אֶת־ הַשְּׁבוּעָ֜ה אֲשֶׁר־ נִשְׁבַּ֣עְתִּי לַאֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֗ם לָתֵ֤ת לָהֶם֙ אֶ֣רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֛ב וּדְבַ֖שׁ כַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וָאַ֥עַן וָאֹמַ֖ר אָמֵ֥ן׀ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Then the LORD said to me, “Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, saying: Hear the words of this covenant and carry them out.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD spoke to me.
The LORD gave me a command.
He told me to speak in the cities of Judah.
He told me to speak in the streets of Jerusalem.
He told me to proclaim all these words.
He said, “Hear the words of this covenant.
Do what these words command.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י קְרָ֨א אֶת־ כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֤ים הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וּבְחֻצ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר שִׁמְע֗וּ אֶת־ דִּבְרֵי֙ הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: For from the time I brought your fathers out of the land of Egypt until today, I strongly warned them again and again, saying, ‘Obey My voice.’
passages.sermon:
God brought the ancestors of Israel out of Egypt.
God began to speak to them on that day.
God continued to speak to them until the present day.
God warned them many times.
God warned them early and often.
God said, “Obey My voice.”
passages.original: כִּי֩ הָעֵ֨ד הַעִדֹ֜תִי בַּאֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֗ם בְּיוֹם֩ הַעֲלוֹתִ֨י אוֹתָ֜ם מֵאֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ וְעַד־ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה הַשְׁכֵּ֥ם וְהָעֵ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר שִׁמְע֖וּ בְּקוֹלִֽי׃

passages.text: Yet they would not obey or incline their ears, but each one followed the stubbornness of his evil heart. So I brought on them all the curses of this covenant I had commanded them to follow but they did not keep.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah and Jerusalem did not obey the LORD.
They did not listen to His words.
Each person followed the stubbornness of his own evil heart.
They refused to do what God commanded.
God had given them a covenant.
He told them to keep its commands.
They did not keep them.
So God brought on them all the curses of the covenant.
passages.original: וְלֹ֤א שָֽׁמְעוּ֙ וְלֹֽא־ הִטּ֣וּ אֶת־ אָזְנָ֔ם וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ אִ֕ישׁ בִּשְׁרִיר֖וּת לִבָּ֣ם הָרָ֑ע וָאָבִ֨יא עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶֽת־ כָּל־ דִּבְרֵ֧י הַבְּרִית־ הַזֹּ֛את אֲשֶׁר־ צִוִּ֥יתִי לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת וְלֹ֥א עָשֽׂוּ׃ס

passages.text: And the LORD told me, “There is a conspiracy among the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
The LORD said, “There is a conspiracy.
This conspiracy is among the men of Judah.
This conspiracy is also among the residents of Jerusalem.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י נִֽמְצָא־ קֶ֙שֶׁר֙ בְּאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה וּבְיֹשְׁבֵ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: They have returned to the sins of their forefathers who refused to obey My words. They have followed other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken the covenant I made with their fathers.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel and Judah have sinned.
They have acted like their forefathers.
Their forefathers refused to obey God’s words.
The people now refuse to obey God too.
They have chosen to follow other gods.
They serve these other gods.
Israel and Judah have broken God’s covenant.
God made this covenant with their ancestors.
passages.original: שָׁ֩בוּ֩ עַל־ עֲוֺנֹ֨ת אֲבוֹתָ֜ם הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר מֵֽאֲנוּ֙ לִשְׁמ֣וֹעַ אֶת־ דְּבָרַ֔י וְהֵ֣מָּה הָלְכ֗וּ אַחֲרֵ֛י אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים לְעָבְדָ֑ם הֵפֵ֤רוּ בֵֽית־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּבֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה אֶת־ בְּרִיתִ֕י אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרַ֖תִּי אֶת־ אֲבוֹתָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD says: ‘I am about to bring upon them a disaster that they cannot escape. They will cry out to Me, but I will not listen to them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel and Judah.
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD says, “I will bring disaster on these people.
They will not be able to escape this disaster.
They will cry out to Me for help.
I will not listen to them.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֤יא אֲלֵיהֶם֙ רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ יוּכְל֖וּ לָצֵ֣את מִמֶּ֑נָּה וְזָעֲק֣וּ אֵלַ֔י וְלֹ֥א אֶשְׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then the cities of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods to which they have been burning incense, but these gods certainly will not save them in their time of disaster.
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah live in many cities.
The people of Jerusalem live in the city of Jerusalem.
These people burn incense to other gods.
They worship these false gods.
A time of disaster will come.
In that time, the people will go to these gods.
They will cry out to these gods for help.
These gods will not save them.
These gods cannot help them in their time of trouble.
passages.original: וְהָֽלְכ֞וּ עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה וְיֹשְׁבֵי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְזָֽעֲקוּ֙ אֶל־ הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥ם מְקַטְּרִ֖ים לָהֶ֑ם וְהוֹשֵׁ֛עַ לֹֽא־ יוֹשִׁ֥יעוּ לָהֶ֖ם בְּעֵ֥ת רָעָתָֽם׃

passages.text: Your gods are indeed as numerous as your cities, O Judah; the altars of shame you have set up—the altars to burn incense to Baal—are as many as the streets of Jerusalem.’
passages.sermon:
Judah, you have many cities.
You have made for yourself many gods.
You have as many gods as you have cities.
Jerusalem has many streets.
You have set up many altars in Jerusalem.
You have made altars of shame.
You use these altars to burn incense to Baal.
You have as many altars to Baal as there are streets in Jerusalem.
passages.original: כִּ֚י מִסְפַּ֣ר עָרֶ֔יךָ הָי֥וּ אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יְהוּדָ֑ה וּמִסְפַּ֞ר חֻצ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם שַׂמְתֶּ֤ם מִזְבְּחוֹת֙ לַבֹּ֔שֶׁת מִזְבְּח֖וֹת לְקַטֵּ֥ר לַבָּֽעַל׃ס

passages.text: As for you, do not pray for these people. Do not raise up a cry or a prayer on their behalf, for I will not be listening when they call out to Me in their time of disaster.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jeremiah.
God told Jeremiah not to pray for the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
God told Jeremiah not to cry out or pray for them.
God said He would not listen to them.
God said He would not hear them when they call to Him in their time of trouble.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֗ה אַל־ תִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ בְּעַד־ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְאַל־ תִּשָּׂ֥א בַעֲדָ֖ם רִנָּ֣ה וּתְפִלָּ֑ה כִּ֣י אֵינֶ֣נִּי שֹׁמֵ֗עַ בְּעֵ֛ת קָרְאָ֥ם אֵלַ֖י בְּעַ֥ד רָעָתָֽם׃ס

passages.text: What right has My beloved in My house, having carried out so many evil schemes? Can consecrated meat avert your doom, so that you can rejoice?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people, whom He once loved.
He asks why His beloved is in His house.
His people have done many evil schemes.
They have acted with wickedness.
They bring consecrated meat into His house.
They think holy offerings will protect them.
God says these offerings cannot save them from judgment.
God says they cannot rejoice because of their evil.
passages.original: מֶ֣ה לִֽידִידִ֞י בְּבֵיתִ֗י עֲשׂוֹתָ֤הּ הַֽמְזִמָּ֙תָה֙ הָֽרַבִּ֔ים וּבְשַׂר־ קֹ֖דֶשׁ יַעַבְר֣וּ מֵֽעָלָ֑יִךְ כִּ֥י רָעָתֵ֖כִי אָ֥ז תַּעֲלֹֽזִי׃

passages.text: The LORD once called you a flourishing olive tree, beautiful with well-formed fruit. But with a mighty roar He will set it on fire, and its branches will be consumed.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Israel and Judah.
He called them a flourishing olive tree.
This tree was beautiful.
Its fruit was well-formed.
The LORD gave it this name.
But the LORD will act with power.
He will send a great noise.
He will set fire to the tree.
The fire will burn its branches.
The branches will be destroyed.
passages.original: זַ֤יִת רַֽעֲנָן֙ יְפֵ֣ה פְרִי־ תֹ֔אַר קָרָ֥א יְהוָ֖ה שְׁמֵ֑ךְ לְק֣וֹל׀ הֲמוּלָּ֣ה גְדֹלָ֗ה הִצִּ֥ית אֵשׁ֙ עָלֶ֔יהָ וְרָע֖וּ דָּלִיּוֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: The LORD of Hosts, who planted you, has decreed disaster against you on account of the evil that the house of Israel and the house of Judah have brought upon themselves, provoking Me to anger by burning incense to Baal.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts planted you.
The LORD of Hosts is powerful.
The LORD of Hosts decided to bring disaster upon you.
He did this because of the evil done by the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
The house of Israel and the house of Judah did evil things.
They made the LORD angry.
They burned incense to Baal.
They provoked the LORD to anger by worshiping Baal.
passages.original: וַיהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ הַנּוֹטֵ֣עַ אוֹתָ֔ךְ דִּבֶּ֥ר עָלַ֖יִךְ רָעָ֑ה בִּ֠גְלַל רָעַ֨ת בֵּֽית־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל וּבֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם לְהַכְעִסֵ֖נִי לְקַטֵּ֥ר לַבָּֽעַל׃ס

passages.text: And the LORD informed me, so I knew. Then You showed me their deeds.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD told me.
I understood because the LORD informed me.
The LORD showed me what they did.
I saw their actions because the LORD revealed them to me.
passages.original: וַֽיהוָ֥ה הֽוֹדִיעַ֖נִי וָֽאֵדָ֑עָה אָ֖ז הִרְאִיתַ֥נִי מַעַלְלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: For I was like a gentle lamb led to slaughter; I did not know that they had plotted against me: “Let us destroy the tree with its fruit; let us cut him off from the land of the living, that his name may be remembered no more.”
passages.sermon:
I am Jeremiah.
I am a prophet.
I was innocent and gentle.
I was like a tame lamb.
People led me to be killed.
I did not know their plans against me.
They made evil plans about me.
They said, “Let us destroy the tree with its fruit.”
They wanted to cut me off from the land of the living.
They wanted my name to be forgotten forever.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֕י כְּכֶ֥בֶשׂ אַלּ֖וּף יוּבַ֣ל לִטְב֑וֹחַ וְלֹֽא־ יָדַ֜עְתִּי כִּֽי־ עָלַ֣י׀ חָשְׁב֣וּ מַחֲשָׁב֗וֹת נַשְׁחִ֨יתָה עֵ֤ץ בְּלַחְמוֹ֙ וְנִכְרְתֶ֙נּוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ חַיִּ֔ים וּשְׁמ֖וֹ לֹֽא־ יִזָּכֵ֥ר עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: O LORD of Hosts, who judges righteously, who examines the heart and mind, let me see Your vengeance upon them, for to You I have committed my cause.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the subject.
The LORD judges righteously.
The LORD examines the heart.
The LORD examines the mind.
I ask the LORD to let me see His vengeance upon them.
I have committed my cause to the LORD.
passages.original: וַֽיהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ שֹׁפֵ֣ט צֶ֔דֶק בֹּחֵ֥ן כְּלָי֖וֹת וָלֵ֑ב אֶרְאֶ֤ה נִקְמָֽתְךָ֙ מֵהֶ֔ם כִּ֥י אֵלֶ֖יךָ גִּלִּ֥יתִי אֶת־ רִיבִֽי׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning the people of Anathoth who are seeking your life and saying, “You must not prophesy in the name of the LORD, or you will die by our hand.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke about the people of Anathoth.
These people wanted to kill you.
They said, “Do not prophesy in the name of the LORD.
If you do, you will die by our hand.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ עַל־ אַנְשֵׁ֣י עֲנָת֔וֹת הַֽמְבַקְשִׁ֥ים אֶֽת־ נַפְשְׁךָ֖ לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֤א תִנָּבֵא֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א תָמ֖וּת בְּיָדֵֽנוּ׃ס

passages.text: So this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “I will punish them. Their young men will die by the sword, their sons and daughters by famine.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD of Hosts is powerful over all armies.
The LORD of Hosts says, “I will punish these people.
Their young men will die by the sword.
Their sons will die by famine.
Their daughters will die by famine.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִנְנִ֥י פֹקֵ֖ד עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם הַבַּֽחוּרִים֙ יָמֻ֣תוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב בְּנֵיהֶם֙ וּבְנ֣וֹתֵיהֶ֔ם יָמֻ֖תוּ בָּרָעָֽב׃

passages.text: There will be no remnant, for I will bring disaster on the people of Anathoth in the year of their punishment.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking about the people of Anathoth.
The LORD says He will bring disaster on them.
The LORD says this disaster will come in the year of their punishment.
No one from the people of Anathoth will remain.
There will be no remnant left.
passages.original: וּשְׁאֵרִ֕ית לֹ֥א תִֽהְיֶ֖ה לָהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־ אָבִ֥יא רָעָ֛ה אֶל־ אַנְשֵׁ֥י עֲנָת֖וֹת שְׁנַ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָֽם׃ס
